Thanks for your answer Matthieu!

In your opinion, are the modifications needed to allow exo variables minor? Or requires a lot of code rewriting?

Jorge Neyro

2013/5/30 Jor ge <jne...@hotmail.com>
> Hi Matthieu,
>
> I'm Jorge Neyro, an economist enrolled in the Master in Economics in the University of Buenos Aires.  I´ve started to do some research last year about Uncovered Interest Parity for the Argentine Economy using Logistic Smooth Transition Regression Models (LSTR) using Matlab. In this type of nonlinear model, I try to explain the rate of depreciation of the local currency (pesos argentinos) using the difference between local and foreign interest rates (exogenous variable). The objetive is to assess the accuracy of the forecast of rate of depreciation in the money market. More details here http://www.aaep.org.ar/anales/works/works2012/Neyro.pdf

Do you know how I can estimate such regression with TsDyn? Should I modify the TsDyn code?
>
> I really appreciate any help you can provide.
>
>
> Thanks
>
>
> Jorge Neyro

messages.subject: Re: Question about TsDyn
messages.body_plain:
Hi

Ok sorry, I was a little bit too quick maybe. If you look at the code of lstar.R, there is a lot of simple data preparation, up to line 90 more or less. Then only the true optimisation procedure starts, giving you the parameters. So this is the part you will be looking at, and you should seek to replace simply the xxL, xxH (line 85-86) and th by your own regressors. Adapting the code from there should require little changes, do not look at lines after 246, since these are specific to tsDyn.

Good luck

Matthieu

messages.subject: Re: TVECM introducing additional regressors (beta0)
messages.body_plain:
Dear Kifle

Ccing to the tsDyn mailing list.

Thanks for your message. There is indeed a beta0 argument, but I must say this is an option I added long time ago, and I am not very satisfied with. I would unfortunately rather sugest not to use it, since the short test I did showed a few issues that cast doubts into the accuracy of this option.

Sorry for this!

Best

Matthieu

messages.subject: Re: TVECM code
messages.body_plain:
Dear Aditi

Ccing my answer to the tsDyn mailing list.

Thanks for your kind word, I am glad tsDyn can be helpful for you!

So regarding point 1), look at the simple regime() function, which gives you a dummy variable indicating the regime. Once applied to your original dataset, this should enable you to estimate two different linear VECM and obtain regime-specific IRF. See also the recent FAQ on this point:
https://github.com/MatthieuStigler/tsDyn/wiki/FAQ

Note however that your separate models do share a common beta, which you could restrict with argument 'beta'.

Regarding the persistence profile, I am not familiar with this unfortunately.

Hope this helps,

Matthieu

2013/6/8 <aditic...@gmail.com>
> Sir,
>
> I am working on a TVECM model for moneatry measures in India. I found your working paper on Threshold Cointegration and the R code for the same very useful.
> However, I had two queries:
>
> 1] Is it possible to extract each regime's model so that I can analyze them separately?
>
> 2] In order to analyze the impulse responses (IRF), is there any option to calculate the nonlinear impulse responses? Or could the individual model IRFs be calculated (using the irf() command) once I can extract the regime-wise models?
> I read in a paper that Persistence Profiles were calculated instead of Generalized IRFs. Can persistence profiles be calculated in R?
>
> Kindly look into the matter.  I shall be grateful to you if you could look into these queries.I would also like to thank you for providing the TVECM code as well as the associated threshold cointegration tests in R.
>
>
> Thanking you
> Yours sincerely
> Aditi Chaubal
>
> _____________________________________
> Sent from http://r.789695.n4.nabble.com
>
